Combined with the earlier reuse of a dead session that returned success with zero turns, the rule for this campaign is: never reuse a GLM session after a timeout or kill; every retry is a fresh attempt on the current tree with the continuation stated in the packet. The take-4 attempt that succeeded for 58 minutes also contains a 971 s silent gap, so on long contexts glm-5.3-flash[1m] can take over 15 minutes to answer and the 900 s stall window kills healthy work. Take 6 raises stallTimeoutSec to 2400 (wall clock stays 7200), keeps GLM flash, tells the worker to read by offset or grep and never whole large files so the context stays small, and states the tree's real condition: check and the fast tests pass, typecheck fails with four errors left by take 5 (listed verbatim in the packet). Three were architectural: nothing committed the worker's edits so an attempt branch carried no work into the candidate (the controller now seals the attempt diff); the integration head could not equal the newest integratedHead because there is no done node at the start or after a failure, the orchestrator may legally commit between attempts and a handoff can reopen a done node (the invariant is now ancestry of every accepted candidate sha over an explicit run ref refs/intent-factory/<run>/run); and ancestry could not identify the transaction to repair because retained attempt branches are ancestors of the tip, an accepted no-change attempt leaves the tip unmoved and an unrelated orchestrator commit satisfies the same predicate (the transaction is now journalled before the ref moves, the ref update is conditional on the recorded previous tip, and recovery replays that record). Partial retrospective at 2026-09-07T16:20Z, phase 0 closed and phase 1 mid-flight. Measured, not recalled: across 7 phase-0 takes there were 18 worker attempts and 11 non-done terminal node states, of which 7 were dependency_failed — 64 percent of the damage was collateral from a sibling node, the exact waste class this campaign exists to remove, reproduced inside the fix campaign because phases 0 and 1 are chained on one mutable tree. The other four were one progress_stalled, two revision_cap and two stall_timeout plus one budget_exceeded. First-attempt success was 0 of 4 logical nodes. Not one failure was caused by wrong work: every one was an operating defect of the 0.2.0 runner or of the orchestrator. What went right and is worth keeping: the persistent watcher closed phase 0 and launched phase 1 inside one hour of the terminal event against dead windows of 5.7, 1.1 and 11.7 hours before it existed; four read-only Astra rounds produced 30 findings, all actionable, and round 4 alone caught two defects that would have broken the phase-1 launch within minutes (empty runtimeRules re-enabling failover synthesis into an OpenAI worker under an OpenAI judge, and both nodes silently inheriting the 300/120/3 progress policy that killed take 1); immutable per-phase controller snapshots let phase 1 run while the tree was mid-edit; the journal and HANDOFF let a cold session resume a 27-hour campaign in minutes. What is being changed now: the recurring defects stop living in notes and become an executable gate, .runs/control/intent-factory-lean-20260905/launch-checklist.mjs, run before validate and preflight on every future phase; and the authoring rules become .runs/control/intent-factory-lean-20260905/PHASE-AUTHORING.md, which every subsequent contract is written from rather than from memory. The checklist was written from the evidence and immediately caught, retroactively on the running phase-1 contract, the one defect Astra missed and the campaign paid for: a Definition of Done gates npm run check and npm run type…

Owner (2026-09-07 13:40 BRT): spend ceilings, in USD or tokens, deliver no value and have interrupted several campaigns; they are impossible to estimate and most operators buy subscriptions with a fixed daily or weekly allowance rather than tokens or dollars. Accepted with the campaign's own evidence: two phase failures were budget_exceeded and none was real overspend, and phase 1 died at 976k raw input tokens because a synthetic 0.1 weight on 44M cache reads crossed a 5M ceiling, a unit nobody is billed in; the cache-read to raw-input ratio across this campaign's attempts ranged from 20x to 54,000x, so the quantity was never estimable. Spec revision 5 (commit a1a8c9c, pushed): rule 3 becomes 'no spend ceiling; time and allowance are the limits' — timeoutSec bounds an attempt, stallTimeoutSec bounds provider silence, usage is recorded for reporting only and nothing is metered for control. Phase 2a turns from implementing maxCostUsd into deleting every ceiling plus progressPolicy and its file-change watchdog. New rule 8 is the owner's requested capability: discover installed drivers and answering models, normalize each provider's exhaustion into {available, exhaustedUntil, reason} including Z.ai 1310 with its reset timestamp, honour a declared assignment exactly, compose an omitted one with the cheapest runtime executing and the strongest cross-vendor runtime judging and planning, and re-tier within a tier on exhaustion instead of descending a cost list. Note the trap for anyone setting usagePolicy false on the 0.2.0 runner: cacheReadWeight becomes 1, not 0, so maxInputTokens must also be raised out of reach.
